criteria.text: Every calculated cell is written as a formula that references its source cells (e.g. "=B5*B6" in openpyxl, or range.formulas in Office JS). No values are computed in Python or JavaScript and then hardcoded into cells.
criteria.source: Core Principles: Every calculation must be an Excel formula

criteria.text: If a template file is attached, the response uses that template's structure and populates it rather than building from scratch. If no template is attached, the response asks whether the user has a specific template before using the standard examples/LBO_Model.xlsx.

The response builds the model one section at a time and stops after completing each major section (e.g. Sources & Uses) to show the result and ask for user confirmation. It does not deliver the full model end-to-end with no checkpoints.
criteria.source: Work section by section / SECTION-BY-SECTION CHECKPOINTS

criteria.text: Sources and Uses balance exactly, with one item (typically sponsor equity) calculated by formula as the plug.
criteria.source: Common Problem Areas: Balancing Sections; Verification: Section Balancing

criteria.text: Debt interest is calculated on the beginning balance to avoid circular references. Debt paydowns or cash sweeps follow the tranche priority order and use MAX/MIN so that balances never go negative.
criteria.source: Interest and Circular References; Debt Paydown / Cash Sweeps

criteria.text: Returns cash flows carry the correct signs (investment negative, proceeds positive). IRR/MOIC formulas reference the complete period range, and MOIC is calculated as total proceeds divided by total investment.

Any sensitivity table uses odd dimensions (5×5 or 7×7). Its axis values are symmetric around the base-case assumptions, and its center cell equals the model's actual IRR/MOIC and is highlighted with #BDD7EE fill and bold font. Each data cell is a formula with mixed references.

Font colors follow the stated convention: blue (0000FF) for hardcoded inputs, black for calculations, purple (800080) for same-tab links, and green (008000) for cross-tab links. Fills use only the blue/grey palette unless the template specifies otherwise.
criteria.source: Formula Color Conventions; Fill Color Palette

criteria.text: When generating a standalone .xlsx file, the response runs recalc.py (or equivalent validation) and confirms there are zero formula errors (#REF!, #DIV/0!, etc.) before delivery. In an Office JS environment, it uses Office JS APIs rather than openpyxl.
criteria.source: Environment: Office JS vs Python; Verification: Run Formula Validation

criteria.text: Number formats follow the stated standards: currency formats, percentages as 0.0%, multiples as 0.0"x", and MOIC as 0.00"x". Numeric cells are right-aligned.
